question: What is the primary document guiding school health efforts in Nigeria?
explanation: The National School Health Policy serves as the official framework guiding health programs in schools across Nigeria. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why are schools considered strategic locations for public health interventions in Nigeria?

options.A: Teachers are legally required to act as primary healthcare providers
options.B: Parents rarely take their children to standard primary health clinics
options.C: Schools have large budgets specifically allocated for medical treatments
options.D: Children spend a large portion of their formative years gathered in one place

explanation: Gathering many children and adolescents in one location makes it efficient to deliver health education, screenings, and preventive services. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core objective of the School Health Program?
explanation: School health programs focus on children and adolescents, not the treatment of advanced chronic adult diseases. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h2)

question: How does early detection of sensory impairments directly impact a student?

options.A: It prevents the impairment from severely hindering academic learning
options.B: It removes the need for teachers to adjust their teaching methods
options.C: It guarantees admission into tertiary educational institutions later
options.D: It completely cures genetic conditions before secondary school begins

explanation: Catching vision or hearing problems early allows for quick interventions like glasses or seating adjustments, protecting the child's education. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h2)

question: Name the three main pillars that make up the traditional school health triad.
explanation: The three core components or pillars of school health are health services, the school environment, and health education. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why must the three components of the school health triad be implemented together?

options.A: A healthy environment reinforces what is taught in class and supported by services
options.B: Health services are too expensive to operate without a clean environment
options.C: Teachers cannot conduct health education without a medical license
options.D: Nigerian law penalizes schools that separate education from sanitation

explanation: The triad works best when classroom teaching matches a clean physical environment and accessible clinical services, creating a unified impact. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of routine medical screenings in schools?

options.A: To detect physical, sensory, or developmental abnormalities early
options.B: To grade students on their personal hygiene practices
options.C: To replace annual visits to family physicians
options.D: To administer mandatory surgical procedures on site

explanation: Screenings are designed to spot hidden health issues like poor eyesight or malnutrition before they worsen. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h4)

question: What action should school health personnel take when a student presents with severe, persistent abdominal pain and fever?

options.A: Administer standard first aid and tell the student to return to class
options.B: Initiate a formal referral to a higher health facility
options.C: Wait until the end of the school term to notify the parents
options.D: Conduct a comprehensive classroom lecture on food hygiene

explanation: Severe symptoms exceed basic first aid capabilities and require urgent professional medical assessment at an established clinic or hospital. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is a key element of the physical school environment?

options.A: Safe drinking water and functional toilets

explanation: Basic infrastructure like clean water and proper sanitation facilities are fundamental requirements for a healthy school environment. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is addressing psychosocial wellbeing considered part of a healthy school environment?

options.A: Teachers are legally classified as psychological counselors
options.B: It prevents physical infectious diseases from spreading among students
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of building maintenance for the school
options.D: Emotional safety and freedom from bullying directly affect learning and mental health

explanation: A safe psychosocial climate protects students from trauma and stress, creating an atmosphere conducive to academic growth. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal of integrating health education into the school curriculum?

options.A: To train every student to become a professional nurse or midwife
options.B: To equip students with practical knowledge to make healthy lifestyle choices
options.C: To replace traditional science subjects with medical training
options.D: To fulfill administrative requirements without student involvement

explanation: Health education gives young people the information and skills they need to protect their health throughout life. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why are participatory teaching methods preferred over passive lecturing in health education?

options.A: Interactive methods require zero preparation from the teaching staff
options.B: Students are more likely to internalize and apply interactive concepts to their lives
options.C: Lecturing is prohibited by the National School Health Policy
options.D: Passive lectures only work for adult university students

explanation: Engaging methods like role-play and discussions help students connect health concepts to real-world personal decisions. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following tasks is typically performed by a nurse or midwife in school health?

options.A: Teaching advanced mathematics to senior secondary classes
options.B: Drafting the national educational curriculum for universities
options.C: Conducting routine health assessments and immunizations
options.D: Managing the financial accounts of the school board

explanation: Nurses and midwives bring clinical expertise to schools by performing health checks, screenings, and immunization updates. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is training teachers in basic first aid an important responsibility for school health nurses?

options.A: It allows nurses to abandon school visits entirely throughout the year
options.B: Nigerian labor laws forbid nurses from treating children directly
options.C: Teachers are present daily and can manage minor emergencies immediately
options.D: Teachers earn extra certification credits for medical procedures

explanation: Since health professionals cannot be on site every hour, training teachers ensures prompt first aid response when injuries happen. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h7)
